raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`load_kv_cache_scales` currently replaces `k_scale` and `v_scale` with Python floats. This raises a `TypeError` when the attributes are registered `Parameter`s, and leaves non-parameter paths with values that tensor-consuming attention backends cannot expand. It also leaves the host-side `k_scale_float` and `v_scale_float` mirrors stale.

Fixes #47357.

## Modifications

- Add a shared helper that updates existing tensor/`Parameter` storage in place, creates scalar `float32` tensors when storage is absent, and synchronizes the host float mirrors.
- Use the helper in all eight model loaders that had the same direct-float assignment pattern: Apertus, Arcee, GLM4, Llama, MiMo-V2, OPT, Qwen2, and Solar.
- Add CPU regression coverage for registered-parameter and absent-scale paths.

The existing per-loader HIP/FNUZ scaling adjustment remains unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

This changes scale representation, not the numeric scale value or model math.

- The issue's checkpoint-free CPU reproduction failed before the patch with the registered-parameter `TypeError` and the missing-tensor `AttributeError`.
- A source-level CPU regression harness against the patched loader passed both paths: existing `Parameter` identity was preserved, missing scales became expandable tensors, and both host mirrors were updated to `0.25`.
- `python -m py_compile` passed for all changed Python files.
- The repository's three registered-test validation scripts passed when invoked directly with Python. The full registered unit test was not run locally because the available Windows environment cannot import SGLang's Unix-only `resource` dependency; it is registered for the upstream CPU CI suite.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. The helper runs only while loading external KV-cache scales, before inference and CUDA graph capture.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (No user-facing interface or configuration changed.)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (Not applicable to model outputs or inference speed; see above.)
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@@ -1932,6 +1932,28 @@ def check_model_type(self, info: ValidationInfo) -> "QuantParamSchema":
         return self
 
 
+def set_kv_cache_layer_scales(
+    layer: torch.nn.Module,
+    scaling_factor: float,
+    *,
+    device: Optional[torch.device] = None,
+) -> None:
+    """Update a layer's device and host copies of its per-tensor KV scale."""
+    scale_value = float(scaling_factor)
+    for name in ("k_scale", "v_scale"):
+        scale = getattr(layer, name, None)
+        if isinstance(scale, torch.Tensor):
+            with torch.no_grad():
+                scale.fill_(scale_value)
+        else:
+            setattr(
+                layer,
+                name,
+                torch.tensor(scale_value, dtype=torch.float32, device=device),
+            )
+        setattr(layer, f"{name}_float", scale_value)
+
+

+import unittest
+
+import torch
+from torch import nn
+
+from sglang.srt.model_loader.weight_utils import set_kv_cache_layer_scales
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+class TestKvCacheScaleAssignment(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_preserves_registered_parameters_and_updates_host_mirrors(self):
+        layer = nn.Module()
+        layer.k_scale = nn.Parameter(torch.tensor(1.0), requires_grad=False)
+        layer.v_scale = nn.Parameter(torch.tensor(1.0), requires_grad=False)
+        layer.k_scale_float = 1.0
+        layer.v_scale_float = 1.0
+        k_scale = layer.k_scale
+        v_scale = layer.v_scale
+
+        set_kv_cache_layer_scales(layer, 0.25)
+
+        self.assertIs(layer.k_scale, k_scale)
+        self.assertIs(layer.v_scale, v_scale)
+        self.assertEqual(layer.k_scale.item(), 0.25)
+        self.assertEqual(layer.v_scale.item(), 0.25)
+        self.assertEqual(layer.k_scale_float, 0.25)
+        self.assertEqual(layer.v_scale_float, 0.25)
+
+    def test_creates_expandable_tensors_when_scales_are_absent(self):
+        layer = nn.Module()
+        layer.k_scale = None
+        layer.v_scale = None
+        layer.k_scale_float = None
+        layer.v_scale_float = None
+
+        set_kv_cache_layer_scales(layer, 0.25, device=torch.device("cpu"))
+
+        self.assertEqual(layer.k_scale.expand((2, 3)).shape, (2, 3))
+        self.assertEqual(layer.v_scale.expand((2, 3)).shape, (2, 3))
+        self.assertEqual(layer.k_scale.dtype, torch.float32)
+        self.assertEqual(layer.v_scale.dtype, torch.float32)
+        self.assertEqual(layer.k_scale_float, 0.25)
+        self.assertEqual(layer.v_scale_float, 0.25)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
